[package]
name = "scrapix-auth"
description = "Authentication primitives for Scrapix: JWT, password hashing, rate limiting"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
license.workspace = true

[dependencies]
# JWT
jsonwebtoken = "9"

# Password hashing
argon2 = "0.5"

# Types
uuid = { workspace = true }
chrono = { workspace = true }
serde = { workspace = true }

# Rate limiting (in-memory fallback)
dashmap = { workspace = true }

version: '3.8'

services:
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v2.51.0
    container_name: scrapix-prometheus
    ports:
      - "9091:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts.yml:/etc/prometheus/alerts.yml:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--web.console.libraries=/etc/prometheus/console_libraries'
      - '--web.console.templates=/etc/prometheus/consoles'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d'
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      - scrapix-monitoring

  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:10.3.0
    container_name: scrapix-grafana
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=scrapix
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=http://localhost:3000
      - GF_INSTALL_PLUGINS=grafana-clock-panel,grafana-piechart-panel
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      - scrapix-monitoring

  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:v0.27.0
    container_name: scrapix-alertmanager
    ports:
      - "9093:9093"
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
      - alertmanager_data:/alertmanager
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml'
      - '--storage.path=/alertmanager'
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      - scrapix-monitoring

volumes:
  prometheus_data:
  grafana_data:
  alertmanager_data:

networks:
  scrapix-monitoring:
    driver: bridge

title: Docker Compose
description: Local development and small production deployments
---

# Docker Compose

Docker Compose is the easiest way to run Scrapix locally or on a single server. The repository includes compose files for both modes.

## Single Binary (Minimal)

The simplest setup — just Meilisearch and Scrapix:

```yaml
# compose.yaml
services:
  meilisearch:
    image: getmeili/meilisearch:v1.31
    ports:
      - "7700:7700"
    environment:
      MEILI_MASTER_KEY: masterKey
    volumes:
      - meili_data:/meili_data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:7700/health"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  scrapix:
    image: ghcr.io/quentindequelen/scrapix:latest
    command: ["all"]
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      MEILISEARCH_URL: http://meilisearch:7700
      MEILISEARCH_API_KEY: masterKey
      RUST_LOG: info,scrapix=debug
    depends_on:
      meilisearch:
        condition: service_healthy

volumes:
  meili_data:
```

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

## Full Distributed Stack

The repository's `docker-compose.yml` runs the full distributed system:

```bash
# Clone the repo and start everything
git clone https://github.com/quentindequelen/scrapix.git
cd scrapix
docker compose up -d
```

This starts:

| Service | Port | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| scrapix-api | 8080 | REST API server |
| scrapix-frontier | — | URL frontier service |
| scrapix-crawler (x3) | — | Crawler workers (3 replicas) |
| scrapix-content (x2) | — | Content workers (2 replicas) |
| console | 3001 | Web UI |
| redpanda | 19092 | Kafka-compatible broker |
| redpanda-console | 8090 | Redpanda web UI |
| meilisearch | 7700 | Search engine |
| dragonfly | 6380 | Redis-compatible cache |
| postgres | 5433 | Auth database |
| clickhouse | 8123 | Analytics database |

### Infrastructure Only

For development, run only infrastructure in Docker and services natively with `cargo watch`:

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d
```

The dev overlay disables all application services and reduces Redpanda memory to 512MB.

Then start services natively:

```bash
just dev  # Uses overmind to start all services with cargo-watch
```

## Development with File Watching

The compose file uses `develop.watch` for hot-reload development:

```bash
docker compose watch
```

This syncs source files into containers and triggers rebuilds on dependency changes:

- **`sync`** — Source code changes (`src/`, `crates/`, `bins/`) synced without rebuild
- **`rebuild`** — Dependency changes (`Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`) trigger full rebuild

## Topic Initialization

The compose file includes an init container that creates all required Kafka topics:

```yaml
init-topics:
  image: docker.redpanda.com/redpandadata/redpanda:v25.3.4
  entrypoint: ["/bin/bash", "-c"]
  command:
    - |
      rpk topic create scrapix.urls.frontier -p 12
      rpk topic create scrapix.urls.processing -p 12
      rpk topic create scrapix.pages.raw -p 6
      rpk topic create scrapix.documents -p 6
      rpk topic create scrapix.events -p 3
      rpk topic create scrapix.dlq.urls -p 3
      rpk topic create scrapix.jobs.status -p 3
```

## Production Considerations

For running Docker Compose in production on a single server:

1. **Change default passwords** — Update `MEILI_MASTER_KEY`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD`, `JWT_SECRET`
2. **Add a reverse proxy** — Use Caddy, Nginx, or Traefik in front of the API
3. **Enable TLS** — Via the reverse proxy
4. **Set resource limits** — Add `deploy.resources.limits` to each service
5. **Configure log rotation** — Use Docker's `json-file` log driver with max-size
6. **Use a `.env` file** — Keep secrets out of the compose file

```yaml
services:
  scrapix:
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2.0"
          memory: 2G
```

## Volumes

The compose file uses named volumes for all persistent data and build caches:

| Volume | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `meili_data` | Meilisearch indexes |
| `pg_data` | PostgreSQL data |
| `redpanda_data` | Kafka topics and logs |
| `dragonfly_data` | Redis cache |
| `clickhouse_data` | Analytics data |
| `cargo-registry`, `cargo-git` | Rust dependency cache |
| `target-*` | Per-service Rust build cache |

To reset all data:

```bash
docker compose down -v
```

## Health Checks

All services include health checks:

- **API:** `GET /health`
- **Meilisearch:** `GET /health`
- **PostgreSQL:** `pg_isready`
- **Redpanda:** `rpk cluster health`
- **DragonflyDB:** `redis-cli ping`
- **ClickHouse:** `wget --spider http://localhost:8123/ping`

title: Authentication
description: User accounts, API keys, sessions, and billing management
---

# Authentication

When `DATABASE_URL` is configured, Scrapix enables a full authentication system with user accounts, API keys, session-based auth, and billing tier management.

<Note>
  All auth endpoints return 404 when `DATABASE_URL` is not set. Without PostgreSQL, the API runs in open mode with no authentication.
</Note>

## POST /auth/signup

Create a new user account. Automatically creates a default account and assigns the user as owner.

### Request Body

```json
{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "password": "[REDACTED]",
  "full_name": "Jane Doe"
}
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `email` | string | Yes | Unique email address |
| `password` | string | Yes | Password (hashed with Argon2) |
| `full_name` | string | No | Display name |

### Response (201 Created)

Sets a `scrapix_session` HttpOnly cookie and returns the user profile:

```json
{
  "id": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "full_name": "Jane Doe",
  "account": {
    "id": "x1y2z3-...",
    "name": "Jane Doe's account",
    "tier": "free",
    "active": true,
    "role": "owner"
  }
}
```

---

## POST /auth/login

Authenticate and receive a session cookie.

### Request Body

```json
{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "password": "[REDACTED]"
}
```

### Response

Sets a `scrapix_session` HttpOnly cookie (7-day expiration) and returns the user profile (same format as signup).

---

## POST /auth/logout

Clear the session cookie.

### Response

```json
{
  "message": "Logged out"
}
```

---

## GET /auth/me

Get the authenticated user's profile.

**Requires:** Session cookie

### Response

```json
{
  "id": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "full_name": "Jane Doe",
  "account": {
    "id": "x1y2z3-...",
    "name": "My Company",
    "tier": "pro",
    "active": true,
    "role": "owner"
  }
}
```

---

## PATCH /auth/me

Update the authenticated user's profile.

**Requires:** Session cookie

### Request Body

```json
{
  "full_name": "Jane Smith",
  "email": "jane.smith@example.com"
}
```

---

## GET /account

Get the authenticated user's account details.

**Requires:** Session cookie

### Response

```json
{
  "id": "x1y2z3-...",
  "name": "My Company",
  "tier": "pro",
  "active": true,
  "stripe_customer_id": "cus_abc123"
}
```

---

## PATCH /account

Update account details.

**Requires:** Session cookie (owner role)

### Request Body

```json
{
  "name": "Updated Company Name"
}
```

---

## API Keys

API keys provide programmatic access to protected endpoints. They are sent via the `x-api-key` header.

### GET /account/api-keys

List all API keys for the authenticated account.

**Requires:** Session cookie

### Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": "k1l2m3-...",
    "name": "Production Key",
    "prefix": "sk_live_abc1",
    "active": true,
    "last_used_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
    "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
]
```

<Note>
  The full key is never shown after creation. Only the 12-character prefix is stored for display.
</Note>

### POST /account/api-keys

Create a new API key.

**Requires:** Session cookie

### Request Body

```json
{
  "name": "Production Key"
}
```

### Response (201 Created)

```json
{
  "id": "k1l2m3-...",
  "name": "Production Key",
  "prefix": "sk_live_abc1",
  "key": "[REDACTED]"
}
```

<Warning>
  The `key` field is only returned once at creation time. Store it securely — it cannot be retrieved again.
</Warning>

### PATCH /account/api-keys/{id}

Revoke (deactivate) an API key.

**Requires:** Session cookie

### Request Body

```json
{
  "active": false
}
```

---

## GET /account/billing

Get the account's billing tier and Stripe customer ID.

**Requires:** Session cookie

### Response

```json
{
  "tier": "pro",
  "stripe_customer_id": "cus_abc123"
}
```

---

## OAuth 2.1

Scrapix also supports OAuth 2.1 with PKCE for third-party integrations and MCP clients. OAuth provides:

- **Dynamic client registration** — Clients register themselves automatically
- **PKCE (S256)** — Secure authorization code flow without client secrets
- **Refresh token rotation** — Automatic token renewal with revocation on reuse
- **Bearer tokens** — For authenticating MCP and API requests

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | OAuth metadata discovery |
| `POST /oauth/register` | Register an OAuth client |
| `GET/POST /oauth/authorize` | Authorization code flow |
| `POST /oauth/token` | Exchange code or refresh token |
| `POST /oauth/revoke` | Revoke a token |

See the [OAuth 2.1 Guide](/guides/oauth) for the complete flow and integration details.

---

## Session Cookie Details

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Name | `scrapix_session` |
| Type | JWT (HS256) |
| HttpOnly | Yes |
| SameSite | Lax |
| Expiration | 7 days |
| Path | `/` |
| Contains | User ID, email |

The JWT is signed with `JWT_SECRET` (set via environment variable or `--jwt-secret` flag).

title: Rate Limiting
description: Per-account rate limits and throttling behavior
---

# Rate Limiting

When authentication is enabled, all API requests are rate-limited using a sliding window counter backed by Redis/DragonflyDB.

## Per-Tier Limits

| Tier | Requests per Minute |
|------|-------------------|
| Free | 10 |
| Starter | 60 |
| Pro | 300 |
| Enterprise | 1,000 |

Unauthenticated requests (when auth is enabled) are limited to **10 requests per minute per IP**.

Authentication endpoints (`/auth/login`, `/auth/signup`) have a stricter limit of **5 attempts per minute per IP**.

## Rate Limit Headers

Every response includes rate limit headers:

```
x-ratelimit-limit: 300
x-ratelimit-remaining: 287
```

| Header | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `x-ratelimit-limit` | Maximum requests allowed in the current window |
| `x-ratelimit-remaining` | Requests remaining in the current window |

## 429 Too Many Requests

When the limit is exceeded, the API returns a `429` response with a `retry-after` header:

```json
{
  "error": "Rate limit exceeded. 60 requests per minute allowed.",
  "code": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "retry_after_seconds": 45
}
```

| Header | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `retry-after` | Seconds until the current window resets |
| `x-ratelimit-limit` | Maximum requests allowed |
| `x-ratelimit-remaining` | Always `0` when rate limited |

## Behavior Details

- **Window:** 1-minute sliding window (60-second TTL)
- **Key:** Per-account (authenticated) or per-IP (unauthenticated)
- **Backend:** Redis/DragonflyDB with atomic INCR + EXPIRE
- **Fail-open:** If Redis is unavailable, requests are allowed through (no rate limiting)

## Handling Rate Limits

Implement exponential backoff or respect the `retry-after` header:

```python
import requests
import time

response = requests.post("https://scrapix.meilisearch.dev/scrape", ...)

if response.status_code == 429:
    retry_after = int(response.headers.get("retry-after", 60))
    time.sleep(retry_after)
    response = requests.post("https://scrapix.meilisearch.dev/scrape", ...)
```

```javascript
const response = await fetch("https://scrapix.meilisearch.dev/scrape", { ... });

if (response.status === 429) {
  const retryAfter = parseInt(response.headers.get("retry-after") || "60");
  await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, retryAfter * 1000));
  // Retry the request
}
```

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'crates/**'
      - 'bins/**'
      - 'tests/**'
      - 'Cargo.toml'
      - 'Cargo.lock'
      - '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
  workflow_call:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUSTFLAGS: -Dwarnings

jobs:
  fmt:
    name: Format
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt
      - run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

  clippy:
    name: Clippy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [fmt]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - run: cargo clippy --all -- -D warnings

name: Deploy to Fly.io

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      force_api:
        description: "Force deploy API"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      force_console:
        description: "Force deploy Console"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      force_workers:
        description: "Force deploy workers (frontier + crawler + content)"
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  group: deploy-fly-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_OWNER: ${{ github.repository_owner }}

jobs:
  # ── Change detection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  detect:
    name: Detect Changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      rust: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.rust }}
      console: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.console }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@v4
        id: filter
        with:
          filters: |
            rust:
              - 'crates/**'
              - 'bins/**'
              - 'Cargo.toml'
              - 'Cargo.lock'
              - 'Dockerfile.fly'
              - 'deploy/fly/**'
            console:
              - 'console/**'
              - 'deploy/fly/console/**'

  # ── Rust build — one multi-target image build per service ────────────────

  check-rust:
    name: Cargo fmt + check
    needs: [detect]
    if: needs.detect.outputs.rust == 'true' || inputs.force_api == true || inputs.force_workers == true
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
      RUSTFLAGS: -Dwarnings
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
      - run: cargo check --workspace

  build-rust:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }}
    needs: [detect, check-rust]
    if: needs.detect.outputs.rust == 'true' || inputs.force_api == true || inputs.force_workers == true
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        target:
          - scrapix-api
          - scrapix-frontier-service
          - scrapix-worker-crawler
          - scrapix-worker-content
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Build and push ${{ matrix.target }}
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: .
          file: Dockerfile.fly
          target: ${{ matrix.target }}
          push: true
          provenance: false
          tags: |
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_OWNER }}/${{ matrix.target }}:${{ github.sha }}
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_OWNER }}/${{ matrix.target }}:main
          # Shared cache across all Rust targets — same dependency graph.
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=scrapix-rust
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=scrapix-rust

  # ── Console build ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  build-console:
    name: Build Console
    needs: [detect]
    if: needs.detect.outputs.console == 'true' || inputs.force_console == true
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Build and push console
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: ./console
          file: ./console/Dockerfile
          push: true
          provenance: false
          tags: |
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_OWNER }}/scrapix-console:${{ github.sha }}
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_OWNER }}/scrapix-console:main
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=scrapix-console
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=scrapix-console

  # ── Fly deploys — one job per Fly app, all parallel ──────────────────────

  deploy-api:
    name: Deploy API
    needs: [build-rust]
    if: always() && needs.build-rust.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: superfly/flyctl-actions/setup-flyctl@master
      - name: Deploy
        env:
          FLY_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLY_API_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          flyctl deploy \
            --config deploy/fly/api/fly.toml \
            --image ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_OWNER }}/scrapix-api:${{ github.sha }} \
            --app scrapix-api \
            --strategy rolling

  deploy-frontier:
    name: Deploy Frontier
    needs: [build-rust]
    if: always() && needs.build-rust.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: superfly/flyctl-actions/setup-flyctl@master
      - name: Deploy
        env:
          FLY_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLY_API_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          flyctl deploy \
            --config deploy/fly/frontier/fly.toml \
            --image ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_OWNER }}/scrapix-frontier-service:${{ github.sha }} \
            --app scrapix-frontier \
            --strategy immediate

  deploy-worker-crawler:
    name: Deploy Worker Crawler
    needs: [build-rust]
    if: always() && needs.build-rust.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: superfly/flyctl-actions/setup-flyctl@master
      - name: Deploy
        env:
          FLY_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLY_API_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          flyctl deploy \
            --config deploy/fly/crawler/fly.toml \
            --image ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_OWNER }}/scrapix-worker-crawler:${{ github.sha }} \
            --app scrapix-worker-crawler \
            --strategy rolling

  deploy-worker-content:
    name: Deploy Worker Content
    needs: [build-rust]
    if: always() && needs.build-rust.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: superfly/flyctl-actions/setup-flyctl@master
      - name: Deploy
        env:
          FLY_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLY_API_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          flyctl deploy \
            --config deploy/fly/content/fly.toml \
            --image ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_OWNER }}/scrapix-worker-content:${{ github.sha }} \
            --app scrapix-worker-content \
            --strategy rolling

  deploy-console:
    name: Deploy Console
    needs: [build-console]
    if: always() && needs.build-console.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: superfly/flyctl-actions/setup-flyctl@master
      - name: Deploy
        env:
          FLY_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLY_API_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          flyctl deploy \
            --config deploy/fly/console/fly.toml \
            --image ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_OWNER }}/scrapix-console:${{ github.sha }} \
            --app scrapix-console \
            --strategy rolling

[package]
name = "scrapix-lifecycle"
description = "Shared process-lifecycle helpers: signal handlers, Fly.io wake listener, idle watchdog"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
license.workspace = true

[dependencies]
tokio = { workspace = true }
tracing = { workspace = true }
